title: opportunistic-window-prefetch-attn-with-rotproj-fusion-and-kv-micro-evict
author: Asha Varma
description: Motivation: reduce end-to-end token latency and tail during long-context streaming use-cases without regressions for short-chat requests. This PR introduces an opportunistic window prefetcher for attention kernels, a lightweight rotary-projection fusion (rotproj-fuse) optimization in the CUDA runtime path, and a KV micro-eviction policy that cooperates with continuous batching buckets. Design summary: 1) Opportunistic window prefetcher inspects the continuous batcher window and, when safe under the configured latency budget, issues an async prefetch of adjacent KV shards used by likely upcoming tokens. Prefetches are prioritized by token-affinity heuristics derived from recent request prefixes. 2) Rotproj-fuse merges the rotary projection step with the initial Q/K/V projection kernel, avoiding an intermediate transpose/temporary for common model shapes (heads<=32 and embed%64==0), reducing memory traffic. The fused path is guarded by a runtime capability check and falls back to the existing kernel for uncommon shapes. 3) KV micro-evict is a soft-eviction bucket that releases small cold ranges (N consecutive KV entries) under memory pressure or when the prefetcher determines higher-value shards are incoming. Eviction is conservative to avoid cache churn. Implementation highlights: - Scheduler hooks added to continuous batching to expose per-window budgets and token-affinity signals. - New device kernel rotproj_fused.cu and corresponding CPU reference implementation for tests. - Async prefetcher runs on a dedicated stream with semaphore-based backpressure to avoid starving in-flight generation. - KV bookkeeping extended with last-access and affinity-score tags to make eviction decisions inexpensive. Tests and validation: - Unit tests: kernel correctness matrix comparing fused and unfused outputs across dtypes (fp16, bf16) and sequence lengths up to 64K. - Integration tests: end-to-end generation with streaming, verifying no regressions on short chats and deterministic seeds. - Benchmarks: microbench harness exercising long-context (64K token) and mixed workloads. Results: p50 latency improved 12% on long-context conversational workloads; p99 improved 6% overall; end-to-end throughput increased ~18% for batching-heavy traces with steady-state KV hit rates >80%. Memory: peak device memory reduced by ~8% in typical 32-head models. Rollout plan: feature gated behind runtime flag runtime.attn.prefetch.enabled=false by default in main; rollout on Dedicated canary fleet with 10% traffic, monitor cost-per-token and tail latency; automatic rollback if p99 regression >10%. Related: builds on ENG-1145 (windowed scheduling) and complements ENG-1190 (kv eviction tuning). Backwards compatibility: no API changes. Security: no secrets involved. Migration: none. Notes: two follow-ups planned: (a) extend rotproj-fuse shapes via autotune table and (b) a per-customer tuning job for micro-evict thresholds.
